battle.name: 呂底亞-米利都戰爭
battle.brief: 公元前628年春，米底王阿斯提亞吉在位第十一年，呂底亞王阿呂阿忒斯舉兵攻米利都，圍城十一年；前625年西密里安騎兵夜襲營地，泰亞提拉之戰勝呂底亞，王中傷次年不治。卡面亞述長弓，即此役西密里安馬上弓箭手所用的近東複合弓形製。

kit.name: 亞述長弓
kit.history: 亞述人靠弓和鐵的組合征服兩河流域。弓兵在車上射，車兵靠弓兵開路。

countries: 交戰方是呂底亞王國與伊奧尼亞城邦米利都。呂底亞方面由國王阿呂阿忒斯（克洛伊斯之父）親自統率，國王駐紮薩爾迪斯，以王室的稅收與奧特曼河一帶的金銀礦脈供應軍費；呂底亞在克洛伊斯時代已把薩爾迪斯經營成愛琴海東岸最富的都邑，軍中同時編有步兵、騎兵與戰車，攻城與野戰並用。另一方是米利都，即伊奧尼亞十二城之首，自公元前七世紀起在黑海沿岸設有奧利比亞、潘提卡佩翁等殖民地，靠雙列三排漿戰船與琥珀金澀錢幣維持一支可觀的海軍，是有錢有船的工商城邦。米利都不是王國而是公民體，由議事會與執政官主政，也有僭主掌握實權，國力不足以與呂底亞陸軍正面對決，因此在圍城同時向斯巴達求援，並把希望寄在北方遊牧的西密里安人身上。第三方包括斯巴達城邦、與呂底亞王族通婚的米底王國（末代國王阿斯提亞吉），以及越過高加索南下的西密里安人。整體形勢是：米利都守城待援，呂底亞以重兵圍城，草原騎兵在戰事後期加入後改變了雙方的平衡。
countriesEn: The belligerents were the kingdom of Lydia and the Ionian city-state of Miletus. On the Lydian side the army was led personally by King Alyattes, the father of Croesus, with the king based at Sardis and the war paid for out of the royal revenues and the gold and silver workings of the Hermus valley; under the house of Croesus, Lydia had turned Sardis into the richest city on the eastern Aegean, and its army combined infantry, cavalry and chariots, using them for field operations and for siege alike. The other side was Miletus, first of the twelve Ionian cities, which since the seventh century BC had founded colonies on the Black Sea such as Olbia and Panticapaeum and sustained a considerable navy of triremes and a currency of electrum staters; it was a rich trading city with money and ships. Miletus was not a kingdom but a civic body, governed by a council and by magistrates, with a tyrant holding the real power in practice, and it was not strong enough to meet the Lydian field army on equal terms. Its answer was therefore to hold the city and wait for help: it appealed to Sparta and set its hopes on the Cimmerians, the nomads of the northern steppe. The third parties were the city-state of Sparta, the Median kingdom, ruled by its last king Astyages and linked by marriage to the Lydian royal house, and the Cimmerians who came south over the Caucasus. The shape of the war as a whole was this: Miletus defended its walls and waited for allies, Lydia pressed the siege with a mass of troops, and the arrival of steppe cavalry late in the struggle changed the balance between the two.
people: 這場戰爭的詳細敘述幾乎全部出自希羅多德《歷史》第一卷十七至二十三節，人物多以王與族群為主。呂底亞王阿呂阿忒斯是克洛伊斯之父，開戰時已在位數十年；他在位第十一年向米利都開兵，圍城十一年，最後在泰亞提拉之戰中受重傷，於第四十在位年傷重不治，長子克洛伊斯繼位，即位時約四十歲。米底王國的末代國王阿斯提亞吉是呂底亞的姻親，他那在位第十一年是希羅多德為這場戰爭定年的錨點，也是其後居魯士崛起、波斯滅米底的起點。率軍夜襲呂底亞營地、在泰亞提拉取勝的西密里安首領，希羅多德明言不知其名，只說他率族人翻越高加索、穿過安納托利亞而來；這支部族與斯基泰人同源，騎射為長，其在呂底亞的劫掠延續到阿呂阿忒斯死後十一年，最後被米底王基阿克薩雷斯驅逐。米利都方面沒有留下將領姓名，留下的是代表城邦出使斯巴達與德爾斐的人：他們依斯巴達之計，在市集懸掛橄欖花冠並宣告多利安人已征服多利安人的城邑，使呂底亞相信神諭應驗而罷兵。凡此可見，這場戰爭的關鍵人物並非某一方的統帥，而是三方合力：呂底亞的持久圍城、米利都的外交周旋，以及北方騎兵的適時介入。
peopleEn: The detailed narrative of this war comes almost entirely from Herodotus, Histories I.17 to I.23, so the people in it are mostly kings and peoples. The Lydian king Alyattes, the father of Croesus, had been on the throne for decades when the war began; in the eleventh year of his reign he took the field against Miletus, besieged the city for eleven years, and was badly wounded at the battle of Thyatira, dying of those wounds in the fortieth year of his reign. His elder son Croesus succeeded him, at about forty years of age. Astyages, the last king of the Median empire and a kinsman by marriage of the Lydian royal house, supplies the anchor for the dating of the war in Herodotus, since it was in the eleventh year of his reign that the war broke out, and he is also the point from which the rise of Cyrus and the Persian conquest of Media follow. Herodotus expressly does not name the Cimmerian leader who led the night attack on the Lydian camp and won at Thyatira, saying only that he came over the Caucasus with his people and through Anatolia; the tribe was closely related to the Scythians, was at home on horseback with the bow, and its raiding of Lydia continued for eleven years after the death of Alyattes, until the Median king Cyaxares drove it out. Miletus left no general's name behind; what it left behind were the men who spoke for the city at Sparta and at Delphi. Following the advice of the Spartans, they hung olive wreaths in the market place and proclaimed that the Dorian had conquered the Dorian city, and Alyattes, seeing them, believed the oracle had been fulfilled and ended the war. The key figures here are therefore not a single commander but a combination of three: the endurance of the Lydian siege, the diplomacy of Miletus, and the timely intervention of northern horsemen.
kits: 卡面這件亞述長弓是公元前八至七世紀亞述人所用的近東複合弓：角、骨、筋合為一體，弓臂短而有力，箭程可及遠處，亞述人靠弓與鐵的組合征服兩河流域，弓兵在車上射、車兵靠弓兵開路。亞述帝國雖在公元前612年滅亡，它始終是這件武器的技術中心，呂底亞王族與亞述的關係極早：呂底亞王吉格斯是亞述王阿淑巴尼拔的進貢者，兩者之間留有現存最早的君主書信，往來涉及安納托利亞西部諸王的臣服與反叛，呂底亞與伊奧尼亞弓兵所用的正是同一近東傳統的弓族，只是形製略作本地化。這場戰爭真正壓迫米利都的用弓者，是馳援來的西密里安人：希羅多德說他們人人善射，裝備形制特殊的弓與短矛，戴獨特頭盔，作戰全在馬背上進行，放箭後即拉開距離，不與敵人纏鬥；這正是亞述弓兵戰法的另一種版本，以騎乘射擊代替車上射擊。雙方其餘裝備也值得一提：米利都的雙列三排漿戰船用於海上襲擾與護航，其步兵持約兩肘長的長矛（希羅多德記載小亞細亞的密西安人如此），並備有雙頭木杆的攻城槌；呂底亞方面除長矛、盾牌與劍之外，還有投石索、青銅片鑲嵌的皮甲，以及本地馬種的騎兵。圍城方在城外維持營壘與壕溝，切斷周邊鄉村的供給。
kitsEn: The Assyrian bow on the card is the Near Eastern composite bow used by the Assyrians in the eighth and seventh centuries BC: horn, bone and sinew worked into one piece, the limbs short and powerful, the arrow reaching a long way, the Assyrians having conquered the river valleys with the combination of the bow and iron, with archers shooting from the chariot and the chariot trusting to the archers to open the way. The Assyrian empire fell in 612 BC, yet it remained the technical centre of this weapon, and the Lydian royal house had very early ties with it: the Lydian king Gyges was a tributary of the Assyrian king Ashurbanipal, and between the two survives the earliest letter of one king to another, the correspondence concerning the submission and the rebellion of the kings of western Anatolia; the bows of the Lydian and Ionian archers belonged to that same Near Eastern tradition, though local forms were worked out. The bowmen who actually pressed Miletus in this war were the Cimmerian horsemen who came to its relief: Herodotus says they were all skilled with the bow, equipped with bows of a peculiar shape together with short spears and wearing helmets of a peculiar fashion, and that they fought entirely from horseback, shooting and then drawing off without closing with the enemy. That is another version of the Assyrian doctrine of archery, with shooting from horseback taking the place of shooting from the chariot. The rest of the equipment on both sides is worth noting as well: the triremes of Miletus were used for raiding at sea and for escort, the infantry carried spears about two cubits long, as Herodotus records for the Mysians of Asia Minor, and double-headed wooden rams were kept in readiness; the Lydians, besides spears, shields and swords, had slings, leather armour reinforced with plates of bronze, and cavalry on native horses. The besiegers maintained a camp and a ditch outside the walls, cutting off the supplies of the surrounding countryside.
tactics: 這場戰爭的戰術主調是圍城加年度進攻，配以馬上射擊的游擊。呂底亞的作法是每年開春揮師進入米利都領地作戰，試圖在野戰中擊潰米利都軍；得手便退回薩爾迪斯方向，因為呂底亞要的是迫使米利都屈服，而不是把城攻破。米利都的守勢則把海港與城牆當作本錢：公民軍在年度會戰失利後退入城中，靠城牆與三排漿船守住入海口，並抓住時機作夜襲反擊。希羅多德記的那一次出城奇襲最關鍵，趁節慶混雜之際突襲呂底亞營地、攻破營牆，呂底亞主將回軍救援才免於全軍覆沒。這是圍城方最接近崩潰的一刻，也說明米利都不是一味挨打。西密里安人加入後，戰術層次立刻拉高：他們不遠征百里，而是整群騎兵藉夜幕逼近營地，以弓矢覆蓋射界、逼迫敵人結陣，再以短矛近身衝擊，在泰亞提拉擊敗呂底亞；得手後連夜進逼薩爾迪斯，卻因準備不足未能破城，只能退回遊牧式的破壞行動，縱掠鄉野而還。呂底亞的對策是據城固守與收縮鄉野，把正面決戰讓給外來騎兵。米利都則靠斯巴達的斡旋與神諭安排的政治出路，讓呂底亞有台階可下。補給上，呂底亞靠薩爾迪斯的金銀產出與遠程征發維持圍城軍隊，米利都靠海運、黑海殖民地與城內儲糧度日，兩條補給線的長短決定誰能撐得久。
tacticsEn: The tactical character of the war was a siege combined with an annual campaign, supported by shooting on horseback. The Lydian method was to march into Milesian territory every spring and try to break the Milesian army in the field; on success they withdrew toward Sardis, because Lydia wanted Miletus to yield, not to be stormed. The Milesian defence treated the harbour and the city walls as its capital: after losing the annual battle in the open, the citizen army retired inside the walls and held the entrance to the gulf with the walls and the triremes, and it was watching for the moment to counterattack. The sortie Herodotus records was the critical one, made in the confusion of a festival, falling on the Lydian camp and breaking its fence, and only the prompt return of the Lydian commander saved the besiegers from total collapse. It was the nearest the Lydians came to being broken, and it shows that Miletus was not simply taking punishment. Once the Cimmerians joined in, the tactical level rose at once: they did not campaign a hundred miles, but brought their whole body of horsemen up under cover of night, covered the shooting lanes with arrows and forced the enemy to form up, and then charged home with their short spears, beating the Lydians at Thyatira. Having won, they came up to Sardis by night, but unprepared as they were they failed to take the city, and could only fall back on nomadic warfare, ravaging the countryside and withdrawing. The Lydian answer was to hold the city, pull the countryside in, and leave the open battle to the foreign horsemen. Miletus, for its part, used the mediation of Sparta and the political escape route that the oracle provided, so that the Lydians had a face-saving way out. As for supply, Lydia kept the besieging army going on the gold and silver of Sardis and on requisitions carried over long distances, while Miletus lived on seaborne supply, on its Black Sea colonies and on grain stored in the city; the length of those two lines of supply decided who could hold out the longer.
data: 可依據的數字有限。戰爭起於米底王阿斯提亞吉在位第十一年，依通行的年代對照約為公元前628年；希羅多德記其延續十一年；呂底亞王阿呂阿忒斯在位第四十年因泰亞提拉之戰所受重傷去世，故一般把這場戰爭定在公元前628至前625年之間，戰事約在前625年收束，次年克洛伊斯即位時約四十歲。西密里安人的劫掠在阿呂阿忒斯死後仍延續十一年，直到米底王基阿克薩雷斯將其逐出（希羅多德第一卷一百零一節）。地理上，米利都到薩爾迪斯直線約一百二十公里，戰役中心泰亞提拉一般認為即今阿克希薩，距薩爾迪斯約五十公里、距米利都約一百六十公里，呂底亞騎兵自薩爾迪斯出擊米利都海岸，單程一日可達。硬體上這是愛琴海東岸最早使用硬貨的年代之一：希羅多德說呂底亞人最早採用金幣，首枚純金幣正出自阿呂阿忒斯在位時，而米利都的琥珀金澀斯塔特自公元前七世紀中葉起流通，說明雙方的軍費都由可抽稅的商業收益支撐。兵力數字則無可靠記載，希羅多德只說呂底亞連年出動大軍圍城而未給人數，任何具體兵員與傷亡估算都屬後人推測。
dataEn: The figures that can be given on good authority are few. The war broke out in the eleventh year of Astyages, which on the usual reckoning corresponds to about 628 BC; Herodotus records that it lasted eleven years; the Lydian king Alyattes died in the fortieth year of his reign from the wounds received at the battle of Thyatira, so the war is generally dated between 628 and 625 BC, closing around 625, and Croesus succeeded the following year at about forty years of age. The raiding by the Cimmerians continued for eleven years after the death of Alyattes, until the Median king Cyaxares drove them out (Herodotus I.101). In geography, the direct line from Miletus to Sardis is about 120 kilometres, and the centre of the war, Thyatira, generally identified with modern Akhisar, lies about 50 kilometres from Sardis and about 160 kilometres from Miletus; Lydian horsemen riding out from Sardis to strike the Milesian coast could make the journey in a single day. In material terms this was one of the earliest ages of hard currency on the eastern Aegean: Herodotus says the Lydians were the first people we know of to use coined money, and that the first pure gold coin was struck in the reign of Alyattes, while electrum staters had been circulating in Miletus since the middle of the seventh century BC, which shows that the war on both sides was paid for out of commercial returns that could be taxed. For numbers of men there is no reliable record: Herodotus says only that Lydia campaigned with a mass of troops year after year to maintain the siege, and gives no figure, so any specific estimate of strength or of losses is later reconstruction.
cause: 近因是米利都不肯歸附。呂底亞在阿呂阿忒斯治下已把薩爾迪斯周邊的希奧尼亞城邑納入稅網，米利都是其中最富、人口最多、海上勢力伸得最遠的一個；希羅多德只說戰爭爆發於阿斯提亞吉在位第十一年，起因是呂底亞在米利都城下的立足點與耕地糾紛，隨即以米利都不肯臣服為由開兵，開戰第一年米利都就在野戰中失利，呂底亞隨即轉入長期圍城。米利都敢於抵抗，是因為它握有海運與黑海殖民地的物資，也因為伊奧尼亞諸城會互相呼應；它不甘心放棄黑海航路的獨占，更不肯被編入薩爾迪斯的秩序。深一層看，這是呂底亞王室的戰略嘗試：用圍城與外交並行的辦法，把一個有海軍的城邦拖入孤立，再迫其低頭；克洛伊斯其後在位時面對的仍是同一道難題。另一個同樣重要的背景是北方草原的壓力，就在呂底亞圍城的同時，西密里安人翻越高加索進入安納托利亞，蹂躪呂基亞、密西安等地後南下半部愛琴海，一場城邦之間的爭端遂變成草原與定居世界之間的撞擊。
causeEn: The proximate cause was Miletus' refusal to submit. Under Alyattes, Lydia had already drawn the Ionian towns around Sardis into its tax net, and Miletus was the richest, the most populous and by far the most seaward of them; Herodotus says only that the war broke out in the eleventh year of Astyages and that it began with a quarrel over the footing and the fields held by Lydians below Miletus, and that it was turned at once into a war of conquest on the pretext that Miletus would not submit, the Milesians losing the first battle in the field in the opening year and Lydia settling down to a long siege. Miletus dared to resist because it held the shipping and the goods of its Black Sea colonies, and because the other Ionian cities answered one another's calls; it was unwilling to give up its monopoly of the Black Sea route, and unwilling to be drawn into the order of Sardis. At a deeper level this was a strategic experiment of the Lydian court: to use siege and diplomacy together to draw a city with a navy into isolation and then force it down; the same difficulty was still waiting for Croesus in his own reign. The other cause, of equal weight, was pressure from the northern steppe. While Lydia was conducting the siege, the Cimmerians came over the Caucasus into Anatolia, harried Lycia and Mysia, and then moved south into the southern Aegean, so that a quarrel between two city-states turned into a collision between the steppe and the settled world.
impact: 直接影響是米利都沒有被攻陷，這在當時的東地中海並非註定。米利都拖到呂底亞撤圍，黑海航路保住，愛琴海東岸第一個真正以海權對抗陸上強權的案例，就此寫下；呂底亞則付出慘重代價：阿呂阿忒斯在位末年戰死，米利都終未收進版圖，國力在圍城中被耗掉十年，而真正的受益者是第三方，西密里安人靠這次介入取得呂底亞西部一帶的劫掠權，遊牧式的掃掠在此後十一年裡反覆折騰薩爾迪斯周邊的鄉野，直到米底人把游牧者趕走才停。長期看，這場戰爭把兩件事推上前台：呂底亞的帝國化嘗試與伊奧尼亞城邦的獨立性正面相撞，幾十年後呂底亞在米利都前碰壁、克洛伊斯王國覆亡，源頭正在此役的未竟與怨恨；呂底亞與米利都之間長期互不信任，幾十年後克洛伊斯仍會再攻米利都。作為武器史的見證，它更標誌著愛琴海東岸的戰爭重心：北方遊牧的馬上弓箭手不再是背景噪音，而是能單獨改寫城邦命運的力量。
impactEn: The immediate effect was that Miletus was not taken, and in the eastern Mediterranean of the day that was not a foregone conclusion. Miletus held out until the Lydians lifted the siege, the Black Sea route was preserved, and the first case in the eastern Aegean of a maritime city standing up to a land power on the strength of its own navy was thereby written. Lydia paid dearly for it: Alyattes died in the last years of his reign, the city was never brought into the kingdom, the strength of the state was spent over ten years of siege, and the real beneficiary was a third party, for the Cimmerians obtained by their intervention the right to plunder western Lydia, and for eleven years their raiding went on against the countryside around Sardis until the Medes drove the nomads away. In the long run the war pushed two things into the open: the imperial ambitions of Lydia collided head-on with the independence of the Ionian cities, and when Lydia was checked before Miletus and the kingdom of Croesus fell a few decades later, the grievance that had begun here was part of the cause; and the distrust between Lydia and Miletus endured, so that Croesus would attack Miletus again in due course. As a witness to the history of weapons, it marks a shift in the centre of gravity of war in the eastern Aegean: the mounted bowmen of the northern steppe were no longer background noise, but a force able on their own to rewrite the fortunes of a city-state.
result: 結果是米利都守住、呂底亞罷兵，但代價已經寫下。前625年前後，泰亞提拉之戰後呂底亞主力受損，王室失去一位在位四十年的君主；克洛伊斯在次年即位，年約四十，接手的是一個在圍城十年裡元氣大傷、又在隨後十一年裡飽受西密里安人劫掠的薩爾迪斯。米利都方面，圍城解除，城邦保住主權與黑海航路，但城外的鄉野損失慘重，收成與稅基都受牽動，另有明確的訊息傳遍伊奧尼亞：海上城邦靠外援可以拖住陸上強權，前提是外援願意來。希羅多德記載的收尾方式尤為耐人尋味：米利都遣使到德爾斐求問神諭，又往斯巴達求援，最後依斯巴達人之計在市集懸掛橄欖花冠並宣告多利安人已征服多利安人的城邑；阿呂阿忒斯見了，以為神諭應驗，於是收兵罷戰、與米利都議和。就全局而言，這場戰爭沒有真正的勝負手：呂底亞用兵十年不能克一城，米利都以一句政治宣告保住了城邦，兩家的舊怨延續到克洛伊斯時代，並在其後更大的衝突中徹底爆發。
resultEn: The result was that Miletus held and Lydia withdrew, but the cost had already been written down. Around 625 BC, after the battle of Thyatira, the Lydian main force was damaged and the royal house lost a king who had reigned forty years; Croesus succeeded the following year at about forty years of age, inheriting a Sardis that had been drained by ten years of siege and then harried for another eleven years by the Cimmerians. On the Milesian side the siege was lifted and the city kept its sovereignty and its Black Sea route, but the countryside outside the walls was badly hit, the harvest and the tax base were disturbed, and a clear lesson was carried through the Ionian cities: a maritime city can hold a land power at bay with the help of allies, provided the allies come. The way Herodotus describes the ending is particularly instructive: the Milesians sent to Delphi to question the oracle and went to Sparta for help, and finally, on the advice of the Spartans, hung olive wreaths in the market place and proclaimed that the Dorian had conquered the Dorian city; Alyattes saw them, took the oracle for fulfilled, and ended the war and made terms with Miletus. Taken as a whole there was no real victor: Lydia had spent ten years of war without taking a single city, Miletus had kept its city with a political proclamation, and the old quarrel between the two ran on into the age of Croesus, where it finally broke out in far greater conflict.
